chunks: Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, who said: He narrated to me from Ali ibn Sayf, who said: He narrated to me from al-Fadl ibn Malik al-Nakha'i, who said: He narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Madani, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from his father, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever comes to visit me during my life or after my death will be in my neighborhood on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the spiritual continuity of the Prophet’s intercession, affirming that posthumous visitation carries the same merit as visiting him in life. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the physical and spiritual presence of the Imams and the Prophet as a means of securing divine proximity (jawar) in the Hereafter.
